title: Graceful upgrade protocol and staged pinning heuristics for model/runtime pairs
creator: Aditi Kapoor
description: Problem: model-serving users see failures or subtle regressions when the serving runtime and model versions change independently. Current routing rules offer coarse pinning and brittle fallbacks which either over-isolate tenants (causing capacity fragmentation) or trigger incorrect model/runtime pairings. Goal: define a graceful upgrade protocol and automated heuristics for staged pinning that negotiate model <-> runtime compatibility, reduce blast radius during upgrades, and provide deterministic fallback behaviors with observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility negotiation protocol documented and implemented in routing layer
Automatic compatibility probe that marks model/runtime pairs as compatible/semantically-unsafe within 12h of rollout
Staged pinning policy applied: canary (1%), phased (10/50/100), and emergency rollback rules
Routing decision logs include pair-version, probe-score, and fallback-reason for every routed request
Operators can run a single command to force pin/unpin a tenant to a version range with audit trail
technical_design: Introduce a compatibility negotiation protocol between the control plane and runtime agents. Each model + runtime build produces a lightweight compatibility descriptor (semantic ABI tags + acceptance test checksum + probe-template). The routing layer evaluates candidate pairings using: explicit pin rules (tenant or route level), descriptor compatibility score, realtime probe health (latency/error diffs), and capacity-aware preference. When scores fall below threshold, routing applies ordered fallback: compatible variant -> older runtime LTS -> safe-generic model build -> degrade-to-API-gateway-queue with autoscaling. A migration-shim service will create temporary translations for KV cache formats and notify runtimes to warm caches for the new pairing. All decisions produce structured logs and metrics consumed by Console rollout dashboards and alerting rules. The design supports a three-stage rollout API (start_canary, advance_phase, abort) with deterministic phases and timeouts.
implementation_notes: Add compatibility-descriptor generation to model onboarding CI
Extend runtime agent to expose probe endpoints and descriptor verification
Enhance routing service to evaluate compatibility scores and emit decision metadata
Build migration-shim service to handle KV cache format negotiation and warming
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal canary on staging with synthetic traffic (24h). Phase 1: 1% production traffic on low-risk tenants, enable probe scoring and auto-abort on regression. Phase 2: 10% then 50% with 4h observation windows and automatic pause thresholds tied to SLO regressions. Final Phase: full migration with background cache warm and capacity ramp. Emergency rollback: immediate re-pin to previous LTS runtime and mark pair as 'unsafe' until manual review.
test_plan: Unit tests for descriptor parsing and scoring
Integration tests for routing decisions with mocked probe responses
E2E synthetic load tests exercising staged phases and migration shim
Chaos tests: inject runtime failures and validate fallback ordering
Canary monitoring runbook with precise SLO thresholds and alert channels
risks: Descriptor mismatch could mark compatible pairs as incompatible and increase cost
Migration shim may not cover all KV cache quirk cases, causing transient errors
False positives from probe scoring could cause unnecessary rollbacks
Increased routing complexity might add latency to decision path if not optimized
